name: Which Location Looks Safer? Raleigh street-view pairs before and after the Great Recession
description:
Method replication: same task, scales and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (78 new Google Street View views of Raleigh, North Carolina: 39 places, each shown from the same direction in 2011–2012 and in 2016, © Google). Based on Freitas, Berreth, Chen & Jhala, "Characterizing the perception of urban spaces from visual analytics of street-level imagery" (AI & Society, 2022). Annotators saw a pair of street views, A and B, and answered five questions on a four-option forced choice (A, B, Both, Neither): which location looks safer, wealthier, newer, better maintained and more occupied. The original collected over 7,200 pairwise ratings on 6,000 pairs of Raleigh images from Mechanical Turk workers in the US and Canada, scored them with TrueSkill, and compared predicted scores with household income in 2011–2013 and 2016–2017. Here each participant rates 10 page-drawn pairs (never two views of the same place); each answer records the two images shown.

Differences from the original study: (1) images are new street views at 39 random places in Raleigh, not the paper's front/back/side views from a 64 km² grid; (2) pairs are drawn at random instead of matched by different feature profiles, and repeated reversed-order pairs are not included; (3) 10 pairs per participant, while the paper does not report how many pairs each annotator rated.
author: Freitas, Berreth, Chen & Jhala
